title: The locus where a local section of an etale sheaf vanishes is the largest Zariski open subset and is detected by geometric points
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma locates the vanishing locus of a local section of an abelian sheaf on S_etale: it is the largest Zariski open subset W of U on which the section vanishes, it can be tested after pullback along any etale map V -> U, and membership of a geometric point of U in W is equivalent to vanishing of the corresponding element of the stalk (statement lines 3942-3963). The proof has three separate steps: existence of the largest W by restriction to the Zariski site (proof lines 3966-3969), the passage from vanishing over V to vanishing over its image using the sheaf condition for the etale covering {V -> phi(V)} (proof lines 3970-3974), and the translation of stalk vanishing into the existence of an etale neighbourhood on which the section vanishes, which then feeds back into the previous step (proof lines 3975-3981). The claim is H2: three short but genuinely different arguments.
